clue.text: Loud report comes from girl Constance held

indicators.note: the short form of the name holds the girl's name within it, like hands gripping it

parts.note: Con is a short form of the name Constance
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl called Constance is detained, and a loud noise results.
explanation.definitionFit: A big gun's firing is the classic booming noise, so the weapon stands for the bang.

clue.text: Leo writhing in little brother's clutches during the dance

indicators.note: the short word for a sibling grips the scrambled name inside it

parts.note: bro is a shortened, informal word for brother

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the name's letters squirm into a new order

explanation.surface: Leo squirms in his kid brother's grasp while they are on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' turns LEO into OLE, which 'clutches' places inside BRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish dance in triple time, made famous by Ravel's orchestral piece.

clue.text: Sheer quality of valuable mine included going over the headland

indicators.note: the first part goes over, that is sits above, the headland in this down entry
the word for valuable takes the word for mine into its middle

parts.note: precious means valuable
a pit is a mine
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A rich mine sits beside a cliff-top promontory, and the drop is alarming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts PIT inside PRECIOUS for PRECIPITOUS; in a down clue 'going over' places that above NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Steepness: the state of a cliff that drops away almost vertically.

clue.text: Leader finds the first performance has been curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a premiere is the first showing of a play or film

explanation.surface: A leading figure discovers the opening night of a show was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been curtailed' drops the final E of PREMIERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister is the head of a government, the leading politician.

clue.text: Unreal projects, buildings without foundations!

explanation.surface: Fanciful schemes are likened to structures lacking footings.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for daydream plans; literally, fortresses floating in the sky have nothing to stand on.

clue.text: Such an entrant cannot expect to be welcomed

definitions.text: Such an entrant cannot expect to be welcomed

parts.words: Such an entrant cannot expect to be welcomed
parts.note: reads like a sour note on a competition newcomer, but describes someone who barges in uninvited

explanation.surface: A newcomer to a contest should not expect a warm reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters without permission, such as a burglar, is never greeted warmly.

clue.text: Manner of speaking of father, say, making clean break

indicators.note: say signals that the word for father is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: break means the letters of the word are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A dad makes a tidy getaway, and his way of talking reveals it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns PA into PAR, which sounds the same in British speech; 'break' rearranges CLEAN into LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular idiom or style of talk, as in legal jargon.

clue.text: Hesitantly follow party worker

indicators.note: the hesitant sound is told to come after the party

parts.note: Labour is a major British political party
er is the noise a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: A party member reluctantly tags along behind the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does manual work for wages.

clue.text: Temper of girl, a trainee

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A young woman, still in training, loses her cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' suggests anger, but here it is the metalworking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To toughen metal or glass by heating and slow cooling, the metallurgical sense.

clue.text: Letters for German banker

explanation.surface: Correspondence addressed to a financier in Frankfurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers' units named after the letter M; also a river in north-west Germany, a 'banker' being something with banks.

clue.text: Telephone system to cover one third of the committee

parts.note: to inter is to bury, covering with earth

indicators.note: a third of the nine-letter word is its first three letters

explanation.surface: An internal phone network is used to brief a third of the panel members.
explanation.definitionFit: An internal two-way communication link, as between rooms of a building.

clue.text: Sensation from the endless stream

indicators.note: endless means the little word loses its end letter

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A brook running on and on is a thing of wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden wave of excitement felt as a tingling feeling.

clue.text: Not understanding violent men pounding her caught inside

indicators.note: the abbreviation for caught is placed within the jumbled letters
violent suggests the letters are thrashed into disorder

parts.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A gang of aggressive men beat a woman who was trapped indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' jumbles MEN POUNDING HER; 'inside' puts C among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to grasp the meaning of something; baffled.

clue.text: Fish to be paid for when delivered

definitions.text: to be paid for when delivered

explanation.surface: A seafood order to be settled on arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: A common food fish of northern seas; also the abbreviation for cash on delivery.

clue.text: Think deeply without time to intervene

indicators.note: without means minus, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: to meditate is to think deeply

explanation.surface: Ponder hard, without delay, before stepping in.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as go-between to settle a dispute.

clue.text: Features a Scottish resort

parts.note: an eye is one feature of the face
a mouth is another facial feature

explanation.surface: A Scottish holiday town gets a mention in the guide.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Features', supplies two facial features in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing town and seaside spot on the Berwickshire coast of south-east Scotland.

clue.text: Insolent, being rash before redhead leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: imprudent means rash, unwise
the head of the word red is R

explanation.surface: Someone cheeky is acting recklessly before a ginger-haired person walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is not a person but the first letter of 'red'; 'leaves' drops that R from IMPRUDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky and disrespectful, showing contempt for others.

clue.text: Let rice hash feed male hawk

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to jumble it, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Allow a rice dish to be fed to the falconer's bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In falconry the male of a hawk, especially a peregrine, is smaller by about a third.

clue.text: Intimidate the animal

explanation.surface: Bully the beast into submission.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat someone into submission; also a female bovine.

clue.text: Pigswill? Nonsense

explanation.surface: Swine feed is just rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally swill fed to pigs; figuratively, rubbish talk.

clue.text: Stay clear of stronghold off the beaten track

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle
out of the way means remote, far from busy routes

explanation.surface: Avoid the remote fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for avoiding something or staying at a distance.

clue.text: Cut out duty

explanation.surface: Abolish the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove surgically; also a tax on goods produced within a country.

clue.text: Exercises included by other mean old creatures

indicators.note: the abbreviation for exercises is placed inside the other letters
other means a different form, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Workouts are done by miserly people in ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges MEAN to AMEN; 'included by' puts PE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive hominids thought to bridge humans and apes, long extinct.

clue.text: Court room is lacking animation

parts.note: to court is to woo a lover
a den is a small private room

explanation.surface: A courtroom is dull and lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff and expressionless, as of a poor actor's performance.

clue.text: Mean to be unhappy

explanation.surface: Being cruel makes you miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemptibly poor or despicable; also deeply miserable.

clue.text: Are confused for a very long time

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the little word's letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: People are bewildered for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or epoch, a lengthy period of history.

clue.text: They are found at sports grounds and in the streets

definitions.text: They are found at sports grounds and in the streets

parts.words: They are found at sports grounds and in the streets
parts.note: covers both terraced seating for spectators and street stalls such as news kiosks or taxi ranks

explanation.surface: Things seen at both stadiums and on city roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectator seating at a ground; also kiosks, stalls and taxi ranks along a street.

clue.text: Miss turns three times

parts.note: spins means turns round
ter is Latin for thrice, used in prescriptions

explanation.surface: A girl pirouettes three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb but is the title for an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman, addressed by the title of Miss.
